articles.title: Two Arrested as Police Recover 11 Laptops, Three Phones in Maseno
articles.desc: Two people are in custody after police recovered 11 laptops and three phones believed to have been stolen in Maseno Township, Kisumu County.
articles.content:
Police in Maseno, Kisumu County, have arrested two people and recovered 11 laptops and three mobile phones believed to have been stolen from university students and other victims.

The National Police Service (NPS) said the operation followed a report made after a laptop was stolen from a hostel room on September 10, 2026. Investigators traced the device to an electronics repair shop in Maseno Township, where the complainant accompanied officers and identified it.

Police said the shop owner told them he had bought the laptop from another person. He subsequently contacted the seller and persuaded him to return to the shop, where officers arrested him.

A search of the seller led to the recovery of another laptop and a mobile phone. Police said the two devices were later confirmed to belong to a university student who had also reported a theft.

Investigators then searched the repair shop, recovering 10 additional laptops and two more mobile phones. According to the NPS, the shop owner could not account for the recovered devices or provide proof of ownership.

The two people are being held at Maseno Police Station pending arraignment. The recovered laptops and phones have been documented and retained as exhibits as investigations continue.

The police service has cautioned members of the public against buying electronic devices from unverified dealers or individuals who cannot provide legitimate proof of ownership.

The recovery also highlights the importance of checking the source of second-hand electronic devices before making purchases. Police said members of the public should report suspicious activities and suspected criminal activity to law enforcement.

The NPS has not said that all the recovered devices have been conclusively linked to particular theft cases. Investigations are continuing as officers establish the ownership and circumstances surrounding the other recovered items. 

The two people will face the next stage of the legal process once police complete their investigations and processing for arraignment.

articles.title: Ruto, Rubio Discuss Trade, AI and Regional Security in New York
articles.desc: President William Ruto and US Secretary of State Marco Rubio discussed trade, AI, critical minerals, energy and regional security in New York.
articles.content:
President William Ruto has held talks with United States Secretary of State Marco Rubio in New York, with the discussions covering trade, technology, critical minerals, energy and regional security as Kenya participates in the 81st United Nations General Assembly.


The meeting took place on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly and comes as Kenya seeks to deepen its economic and strategic engagement with the United States. Ruto said the Kenya-US relationship remains anchored on trade, security, technology and development.


Trade was among the issues discussed, with Ruto welcoming the extension of the African Growth and Opportunity Act (AGOA). He said the move would strengthen trade between Africa and the United States and create wider economic opportunities.


The two sides also discussed cooperation in emerging technologies, particularly artificial intelligence. According to the reporting on the meeting, the talks included the use of AI in areas such as health, education and financial services, as well as the responsible governance of rapidly developing AI technologies.


Critical minerals and nuclear energy were also part of the discussions, adding strategic-resource and energy cooperation to the Kenya-US agenda.


Regional security featured alongside the economic issues. Ruto and Rubio discussed efforts to sustain the security mission in Somalia, support stability in Haiti and respond to the worsening humanitarian situation in Sudan.


The Sudan discussions included efforts toward a ceasefire, a political settlement and continued regional engagement, according to the report on the meeting.


The talks form part of Kenya's wider engagement during the UN General Assembly high-level week in New York. Kenya's Permanent Mission to the United Nations lists September 22 as the opening day of the General Debate for the 81st session, bringing heads of state and government together to address major international issues.


For Kenyan readers, the discussions touch on areas with potential implications beyond diplomacy, particularly trade opportunities, technology cooperation, energy and the country's role in regional security.


Ruto is continuing Kenya's engagements in New York as the high-level UN General Assembly programme gets underway.

articles.title: Government Steps Up Response as Swine Fever Hits Seven Counties
articles.desc: Kenya has intensified livestock disease surveillance after African Swine Fever outbreaks were reported in seven counties, with 1,470 pigs dead in Kiambu.
articles.content:
The government has stepped up measures to contain African Swine Fever (ASF) after significant outbreaks were reported across seven counties, raising concern over the further spread of the highly contagious disease.

The latest update from the Department of Veterinary Services shows that outbreaks have been reported in Kiambu, Tharaka-Nithi, Busia, Embu, Kakamega, Homa Bay and Migori.

Kiambu has recorded the largest reported losses, with more than 1,470 pigs dying across over 20 farms since mid-May. The outbreak has affected farms in areas including Juja, Thika and Ruiru.

In Tharaka-Nithi, the veterinary authorities recorded 108 cases and 97 deaths between January 5 and 11, according to the latest government information presented to the Border Control and Operations Coordination Committee.

The government says the spread across multiple counties has widened concerns about transmission and prompted stronger livestock disease surveillance, prevention and response measures.

Authorities are also monitoring the movement of livestock and pastoralist communities, particularly in connection with cross-border movement, as part of efforts to prevent further transmission.

The development comes as Kenya seeks to grow its pig industry, making disease control an important issue for farmers whose livelihoods depend on pig production.

African Swine Fever is highly contagious among pigs and can cause severe losses on affected farms. It does not infect humans, according to the World Organisation for Animal Health.

For farmers, the latest government response places greater emphasis on early detection, disease surveillance and measures that can limit the movement of infection between farms and counties.

The government has not indicated that the disease poses a direct public-health threat to people. The immediate concern is its potential impact on pig farmers, livestock production and livelihoods if transmission continues.

articles.title: Ruto Signs Four Bills, Changing Rules on Kenya's Public Finances and Trusts
articles.desc: President Ruto has signed four Bills into law, introducing new rules on public finance, air passenger charges, population planning and trusts.
articles.content:
President William Ruto has assented to four Bills into law at State House, Nairobi, introducing new legal frameworks covering public finance management, air passenger charges, population planning and trust administration. The President signed the legislation on Tuesday, September 8, 2026.

The four laws are the Public Finance Management Amendment Bill 2025, Air Passenger Service Charge Amendment Bill, National Council for Population and Development Bill and Trust Administration Bill. Their enactment gives the legislation the force of law after passage through Parliament.

One of the significant changes is contained in the Public Finance Management Amendment law, which seeks to strengthen accountability in the handling of public funds. The amendments introduce penalties for public entities that fail to act on recommendations arising from reports by the Auditor-General and Controller of Budget, including findings adopted by Parliament or county assemblies.

The legislation also shortens the period within which public entities are required to submit financial statements, putting greater emphasis on timely financial reporting and follow-up on audit findings.

Another law changes the framework governing air passenger service charges. The amendments provide for the distribution of proceeds to institutions including the Kenya Airports Authority, Kenya Civil Aviation Authority, Kenya Meteorological Department and Tourism Fund.

For population planning, the new National Council for Population and Development law establishes the council as a statutory body responsible for coordinating population policies and supporting evidence-based planning on demographic and development issues.

The fourth law, the Trust Administration Act, creates a consolidated legal framework for the administration of trusts. It replaces separate laws governing trustees and seeks to reduce duplication and inconsistencies in the management of trusts and related assets.

The signing means the four measures have now moved beyond Parliament and into the implementation stage. Their practical effect will depend on how the relevant government agencies and institutions apply the new legal provisions.

For Kenyans, the changes could have implications ranging from the oversight of public money and management of government finances to aviation-related charges and the administration of trusts and assets.

The four new Kenyan laws signed by President Ruto today therefore mark another step in the government's ongoing changes to public finance, governance and regulatory frameworks.

articles.title: Government Releases KSh850 Million Cash Support for Vulnerable Families
articles.desc: The government has released KSh850.7 million to support more than 425,000 households caring for orphans and vulnerable children.
articles.content:
The government has released more than KSh850 million to support households enrolled in the Cash Transfer for Orphans and Vulnerable Children programme under the Inua Jamii social protection initiative.

Gender, Culture and Children Services Cabinet Secretary Hanna Wendot Cheptumo announced the latest disbursement on Wednesday, saying a total of KSh850,696,000 had been allocated to 425,348 beneficiary households across the country.

Under the payment cycle, each eligible household is set to receive KSh2,000 for the July 2026 payment.

The funds are intended to support families caring for orphans and vulnerable children, helping them meet basic household needs and provide care for children living in vulnerable circumstances.

According to the announcement, payments began on September 1 through the government's contracted Payment Service Provider.

The latest release provides fresh support to families who depend on social protection programmes to help meet everyday expenses.

For many vulnerable households, cash assistance can help with essential needs such as food, clothing and other basic requirements, particularly at a time when many families continue to face pressure from the cost of living.

The Cash Transfer for Orphans and Vulnerable Children programme is implemented through the State Department for Children Services as part of the wider Inua Jamii initiative.

Inua Jamii is among the government's key social protection programmes and is designed to provide financial assistance to eligible vulnerable groups and households.

The latest disbursement focuses specifically on households caring for orphans and vulnerable children, with more than 425,000 households included in the current payment cycle.

Beneficiaries have also been urged to follow the established payment procedures when accessing their funds and remain alert to fraudsters who may attempt to take advantage of the disbursement.

The announcement is likely to bring relief to families awaiting the payment, particularly those who rely on the support to supplement their household income.

As payments continue, attention will now turn to ensuring that eligible beneficiaries receive their funds smoothly and without unnecessary delays.

The latest release also highlights the continued role of cash transfer programmes in supporting vulnerable families and cushioning households facing financial challenges across Kenya.

articles.title: Principals Warn Funding Shortfall Could Disrupt Learning in Schools
articles.desc: Secondary school principals warn that a capitation funding shortfall could disrupt learning as schools begin the third term
articles.content:
Secondary school principals have raised fresh concerns over government capitation, warning that continued funding shortfalls could disrupt learning as schools begin the third term.

The concerns were raised on Tuesday by the Kenya Secondary Schools Heads Association, whose chairperson Willie Kuria said many institutions were struggling to meet their financial obligations because they had not received the full annual capitation allocation per learner.

According to the principals, the government is expected to provide KSh22,244 annually for each learner. However, schools say the funds available to them remain below that amount, leaving administrators under pressure as they run academic programmes and meet essential expenses.

The funding concerns come only days after learners returned for the third term, a critical period for schools preparing candidates for national examinations.

School heads say inadequate funding affects their ability to pay for essential services and supplies, including food, water, electricity and other day-to-day operations.

The issue has also raised questions about the difference between funds announced as released by the government and the actual amount that reaches individual school accounts.

Kuria said some of the money is retained for specific education-related activities, meaning the amount available directly to school administrators can be lower than the figure publicly announced as released.

For parents and learners, the concern is whether the funding gap could eventually interfere with normal learning activities if schools continue struggling to meet operational costs.

The warning also places renewed attention on the wider challenge of financing public education at a time when the cost of food, utilities and other essential services has increased.

Education funding has remained a major concern for school administrators, particularly where institutions must continue operating even when capitation is delayed or falls below expected levels.

The principals are now calling for the government to address the shortfall and ensure schools receive adequate funding to run their programmes without disruption.

As the third term continues, attention will be on whether additional funds are released and whether the concerns raised by school heads can be resolved before the financial pressure affects learners more directly.

articles.title: CA Proposes New Safeguards for Recycling Inactive Mobile Numbers
articles.desc: The Communications Authority has proposed safeguards for inactive mobile numbers as Kenyans are invited to submit public views.
articles.content:
The Communications Authority of Kenya has opened public consultation on proposed safeguards that could change how inactive mobile phone numbers are deactivated and later recycled.

The draft procedures are intended to guide the handling of inactive telecommunication numbers while protecting the rights and interests of subscribers.

The Communications Authority says the framework is needed to help manage Kenya's numbering resources, which must remain available as demand for telecommunications services continues to grow.

The proposal is particularly important because mobile numbers have become closely connected to people's digital lives.

A phone number can be linked to mobile money, banking services, messaging platforms, social media accounts and other online services. Reassigning a number without proper safeguards could therefore create privacy and security concerns for a former subscriber.

The draft rules come after a High Court ruling that highlighted the importance of protecting mobile numbers as part of a person's digital identity.

The Communications Authority has invited members of the public and other stakeholders to submit their views before the proposed safeguards are finalised.

For ordinary mobile users, the consultation provides an opportunity to raise concerns about what should happen when a SIM card or mobile number becomes inactive.

The proposed framework is not simply about taking unused numbers out of circulation. It is also expected to establish clearer procedures for how numbers are handled before they are eventually made available to another user.

The issue matters because Kenya depends heavily on mobile communication and mobile-based financial services. A number that appears inactive may still have connections to important accounts or personal information.

Clear safeguards could therefore help reduce the risk of privacy breaches while allowing the country to manage its limited pool of mobile numbers more efficiently.

The Communications Authority has made the draft procedures available through its Open Consultations platform and is seeking public feedback before the final framework is adopted.

As the consultation continues, attention will focus on whether the proposed safeguards provide sufficient protection for subscribers while also meeting the growing demand for mobile numbering resources.

articles.title: Kenya Railways Adds Special Trains as Aviation Disruptions Continue
articles.desc: Kenya Railways has added special Nairobi–Mombasa services, giving travellers more options as aviation disruptions continue.
articles.content:
Kenya Railways has introduced additional special train services between Nairobi and Mombasa, offering travellers more options as disruptions continue to affect the aviation sector.

The extra Madaraka Express services were announced on Monday and will operate over August 31 and September 1.

Kenya Railways said the additional trips are available for booking and encouraged passengers to reserve seats early.

The move comes as aviation disruptions have left many travellers facing delayed, cancelled or rescheduled flights. For passengers who still need to travel between Nairobi and Mombasa, the additional rail services provide another transport option during the disruption.

According to the announced schedule, a special train was set to depart Mombasa Terminus at 8:40pm on Monday. On Tuesday, additional services are scheduled from Nairobi Terminus at 9:40am and Mombasa Terminus at 4:30pm.

The development is particularly relevant to travellers whose plans have been affected by the ongoing disruption in airport operations.

For many passengers, transport disruptions can lead to missed connections, cancelled meetings and unexpected accommodation costs. The availability of extra train services could therefore help ease some of the pressure on travellers seeking to move between Kenya's capital and the Coast.

The announcement also highlights the importance of alternative transport networks when a major sector faces disruption.

Passengers planning to use the additional services have been advised to make bookings early because demand may increase as more travellers look for alternatives to air travel.

For now, the special services offer a practical option for people travelling along one of Kenya's busiest transport corridors while aviation operations remain under pressure

articles.title: KUCCPS Reopens KMTC Applications, Giving Students Another Chance
articles.desc: KUCCPS has reopened applications for selected KMTC programmes, giving eligible students another chance to join the September 2026 intake.
articles.content:
Students seeking to join the Kenya Medical Training College have received another opportunity after the Kenya Universities and Colleges Central Placement Service reopened applications for selected programmes ahead of the September 2026 intake.

The latest application window gives eligible candidates another chance to compete for available places, particularly those who missed an earlier opportunity or were unable to secure placement.

The reopening is significant for students hoping to pursue careers in Kenya's health sector, where KMTC remains one of the country's key training institutions for medical and health-related professionals.

For many young people and their families, missing an application deadline can delay education and career plans. A reopened window can therefore provide a fresh opportunity for candidates still seeking placement.

Reports published Monday indicate that selected diploma and certificate programmes are available under the latest application exercise, with applicants expected to use the KUCCPS student portal.

The opportunity also highlights the importance of students checking programme requirements carefully before submitting their choices. Different courses have different entry qualifications, meaning candidates should ensure their KCSE results meet the requirements for their preferred programmes.

Applicants should also confirm the availability of programmes and follow official KUCCPS instructions when submitting applications.

The development matters beyond the students applying today. Access to medical training helps prepare future health workers who may eventually serve communities across Kenya.

For families with students still searching for education opportunities, the reopened application window offers another pathway into professional training rather than waiting for a future intake.

The key message for eligible applicants is to act within the available application period and rely on official KUCCPS information when making their choices.

As the September 2026 intake approaches, the reopening gives students with an interest in medical and health-related careers another chance to secure a place in training.

articles.title: Milk Supply Pressure Raises Price Concerns as COFEK Calls for Action
articles.desc: Falling formal milk supplies have raised price concerns as COFEK gives the government seven days to outline urgent action.
articles.content:
Kenyans could face increased pressure on milk prices after formal-sector supplies declined, prompting the Consumers Federation of Kenya to demand urgent government action.

New data cited by COFEK shows that formal milk intake fell from 88.89 million litres in May to 84.44 million litres in June, a five per cent month-to-month decline.

The consumer body has now called on the government to outline measures within seven days to address supply challenges and protect consumers from further price increases.

The issue is already being felt in parts of the market. COFEK says some retailers in Nairobi have begun rationing purchases, while fresh milk prices at some outlets have increased.

For households, milk is an everyday commodity, meaning changes in supply and prices can quickly affect family budgets. The situation also affects retailers and dairy farmers who depend on a stable market.

Smallholder farmers, who provide a major share of Kenya's milk supply, are facing pressure from reduced pasture availability and rising animal-feed costs, according to COFEK.

The federation says some farmers have reported lower milk yields, adding to concerns about the stability of supply if the challenges continue.

COFEK has called for coordinated action involving the Ministry of Agriculture, the Kenya Dairy Board and the National Treasury. Its demands include a recovery plan, support to affected dairy farmers and closer monitoring of retail prices.

The development has also renewed attention on Kenya's ability to manage milk shortages after periods of surplus production.

For consumers, the key question is whether action can stabilise supply before shortages become more widespread and prices rise further.

The government's response in the coming days will therefore be closely watched by households, farmers and businesses across the dairy sector.
